articles.title: Fauci Perjury Exposed: Rand Paul Demands DOJ Prosecute NIH Chief for Lying to Congress on Gain-of-Function
articles.summary: Senator Rand Paul has formally requested a DOJ investigation into Anthony Fauci for alleged perjury during 2021 congressional testimony regarding NIH funding of gain-of-function research at the Wuhan Institute of Virology. Paul contends Fauci knowingly misled Congress while documentary evidence — including NIH grant records — directly contradicts his sworn statements. If prosecuted, this would represent the most significant accountability moment for federal public health leadership in modern history.

articles.title: Fauci's Private Diary Surfaces: Trashed Trump, Praised Beijing, Lost Classified Files in Ransomware Attack
articles.summary: Newly released diary pages from Anthony Fauci reveal a pattern of political bias, admiration for Chinese health officials, and a catastrophic breach — the loss of confidential government records in a ransomware hack. These entries directly undercut Fauci's public posture of apolitical scientific neutrality during the COVID-19 pandemic. The diary adds damning personal context to congressional allegations that Fauci's leadership was compromised by ideology and institutional failure.

articles.title: Cheap Off-Patent Drugs Are Beating Cancer — And Oncology's Profit Machine Is Burying the Evidence
articles.summary: Dr. William Makis, a Canadian oncologist and vocal dissident, is documenting the anti-cancer potential of repurposed off-patent drugs including ivermectin — compounds that cannot be monetized and therefore receive no industry-funded trial support. The standard oncology pipeline systematically ignores these agents because they threaten billion-dollar chemotherapy and immunotherapy revenue streams. Patients dying on approved protocols are never told these alternatives exist.

articles.title: Antidepressants: The Benefits Are Overstated, the Harms Are Buried — A Reckoning Begins
articles.summary: A critical scientific analysis of antidepressant medications confronts decades of inflated efficacy claims and systematically underreported adverse effects — from sexual dysfunction to emotional blunting to withdrawal syndromes misclassified as relapse. These drugs are now prescribed to hundreds of millions worldwide, yet the evidence base supporting their use for mild-to-moderate depression is far weaker than regulators and prescribers acknowledge. The replication crisis in psychiatric pharmacology remains largely hidden from patients.

articles.title: Medical Device Maker Hid Safety Failures From Investors — FDA Compliance Theater Exposed in Beta Bionics Fraud Case
articles.summary: Beta Bionics allegedly misled investors about the safety, efficacy, and commercial viability of its iLet insulin delivery device, triggering a 37% stock collapse and a securities fraud class action lawsuit. The case exposes how FDA compliance processes can be gamed to project regulatory approval while concealing real-world device failures. When the truth surfaced, it was investors — not patients — who triggered accountability.

articles.title: COVID Billing Fraud: Plano Clinics Pocketed $20 Million Billing Nasal Swabs as Full Office Visits
articles.summary: A network of COVID testing clinics in Plano, Texas has agreed to pay $20 million to settle allegations that routine nasal swab tests were systematically billed as physician office visits — a scheme that defrauded federal pandemic relief programs. The settlement is a window into the broader ecosystem of COVID-era medical grift that was enabled by emergency funding with minimal oversight. The perpetrators operated for months before enforcement caught up.

articles.title: Epstein Whistleblower Who Exposed Commerce Secretary's Ties Dies by Suicide — Investigators Demand Probe
articles.summary: Simon Andriesz, the British whistleblower who publicly exposed financial links between Jeffrey Epstein and U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, has died by suicide — triggering immediate calls for an independent investigation into his treatment by UK regulators prior to his death. Andriesz went public on record just weeks before his death, making the timing deeply suspicious to fellow researchers and civil liberties advocates. The pattern of whistleblowers dying under ambiguous circumstances after exposing powerful institutional figures demands systemic scrutiny.

articles.title: Mebendazole Suppresses Drug-Resistant Lung Cancer — Another Off-Patent Drug the Oncology Cartel Won't Trial
articles.summary: A peer-reviewed PLOS ONE study demonstrates that mebendazole, a decades-old antiparasitic drug costing cents per dose, significantly suppresses tumor growth in gefitinib-resistant non-small cell lung cancer by dual-targeting EGFR signaling and microtubule dynamics. Despite compelling preclinical evidence, no major cancer institution is funding large-scale human trials — because mebendazole is off-patent and offers no return on investment for pharmaceutical sponsors. Patients with treatment-resistant lung cancer are being denied access to data that already exists.

articles.title: Fauci Perjury File: Rand Paul Demands DOJ Investigate Whether America's COVID Czar Lied to Congress About Gain-of-Function Funding
articles.summary: Senator Rand Paul has formally referred Dr. Anthony Fauci to the Department of Justice for alleged perjury during 2021 congressional testimony, asserting Fauci knowingly misled Congress when he denied NIH funding of gain-of-function research at the Wuhan Institute of Virology. This is the unfiltered Fauci the press refused to show you for four years.

articles.title: The Antidepressant Reckoning: What the Science Actually Shows About Benefits, Harms, and a Nation Hooked on Pills
articles.summary: A rigorous examination of the antidepressant evidence base reveals a medication class prescribed to tens of millions whose mechanisms remain poorly understood and whose harm profile — including dependence, sexual dysfunction, and withdrawal — is routinely minimized by prescribers. The chemical imbalance theory that sold a generation on SSRIs has been quietly walked back by its own proponents, yet prescriptions continue to climb. The gap between what doctors tell patients and what the data shows is a scandal hiding in plain sight.

articles.title: Off-Patent, Cheap, and Effective: Why Dr. Makis Says Repurposed Drugs Like Ivermectin Could Upend Cancer Care — and Why Oncology Won't Touch Them

Peer-reviewed literature supports plausible anti-tumor activity, yet no major cancer center is running the trials. When a drug can't be patented, patients don't get the research — that is pharma capture in its purest form.

articles.title: Medical Device Maker Beta Bionics Accused of Hiding Safety Failures From Investors — FDA Compliance Problems Trigger Securities Fraud Lawsuit

Investors allege company executives knowingly misrepresented the device's safety record and commercial trajectory while the problems mounted. When medical device companies hide safety data from markets, patients and investors both pay the price.

articles.title: Repurposed Cancer Drug Mebendazole Suppresses Gefitinib-Resistant Lung Tumors — Science Big Pharma Won't Fund Because It Costs Pennies
articles.summary: A peer-reviewed study in PLOS ONE demonstrates that mebendazole, a decades-old antiparasitic costing cents per dose, disrupts microtubule dynamics and significantly suppresses tumor growth in gefitinib-resistant non-small cell lung cancer — one of oncology's most lethal dead ends. The mechanism is biologically coherent and the results are striking, yet no pharmaceutical company will fund the trials needed to bring this to patients because there is no patent revenue to capture. Science that saves lives but makes no money gets buried.
